# openpilot-xnor-bis — Technical Reference

*A code-verified reverse-engineering reference for the `openpilot-xnor-bis` repository (comma.ai's `openpilot`), generated by reading the actual source rather than the README/docs. Every claim below is tagged, implicitly or explicitly, as **confirmed from code**, ***strong inference***, or **uncertain**; discrepancies between documentation/comments and actual behavior are called out inline and rolled up in the [Documentation vs. Code Discrepancies](#documentation-vs-code-discrepancies-rollup) section.*

**Scope**: exhaustive coverage of `selfdrive/`, `system/`, `common/`, and `cereal`'s Python messaging API; interface-level coverage of vendored sibling repositories (`opendbc_repo`, `panda`, `msgq_repo`, `rednose_repo`, `tinygrad_repo`, `teleoprtc_repo`, `third_party`); summary-level coverage of `tools/`. All file paths are relative to the repository root.

**Repository snapshot**: not a git repository at analysis time (no `.git` directory) — no commit history, blame, or upstream diff was available. Latest recorded release per `RELEASES.md`: 0.11.1 (2026-04-08).

## 1. Executive Summary

**openpilot-xnor-bis** is a local checkout of **comma.ai's `openpilot`**, an open-source "operating system for robotics" that implements an ADAS (Advanced Driver-Assistance System) — adaptive cruise control + lane centering — for 275+ supported production cars, running on comma's own hardware (the "comma 3X", codename `tici`) or on a PC for development/simulation. No xnor-specific fork markers, custom branding, or divergent business logic were found in the files inspected; the directory name is the only fork-specific artifact observed (**uncertain** — a full diff against upstream `commaai/openpilot` was not performed since this is not a git repository here, i.e. there is no `.git` directory, so history/blame is unavailable).

Confirmed from code: the system is a **fleet of ~35 independent OS processes** ("daemons"), supervised by a single Python process manager (`system/manager/manager.py`), that communicate exclusively through a pub/sub shared-memory messaging bus (`cereal`, capnp-schema based). There is no monolithic "main loop" — the architecture is a real-time distributed pipeline: camera capture → neural-net driving-policy inference → planning → low-level control → CAN bus actuation, running alongside parallel localization, logging, UI, and telemetry pipelines, all at fixed rates (typically 20-100Hz for the driving-critical path).

### Major subsystems and how they communicate

All inter-process communication is via **cereal** (`cereal/messaging`), a capnp-schema pub/sub bus over shared memory (`msgq_repo`, vendored, interface documented in the Messaging section). No subsystem calls another directly in-process except within a single daemon; every cross-daemon interaction is a message publish/subscribe pair. This is confirmed by the `messaging.SubMaster`/`PubMaster` usage pattern found throughout every daemon covered below.

- **Perception** (`selfdrive/modeld`, `system/camerad`, `selfdrive/monitoring`) — turns camera frames into a driving trajectory + object list, and a driver-attention state.
- **Localization** (`selfdrive/locationd`) — fuses IMU/GPS/CAN/vision odometry into a Kalman-filtered pose, plus online estimation of vehicle-specific control parameters (steering ratio, tire stiffness, actuator lag).
- **Control stack** (`selfdrive/controls`, `selfdrive/selfdrived`) — radar tracking, longitudinal/lateral trajectory planning, the high-level state machine (engaged/disengaged, alerts), and the low-level controller that turns plans into actuator commands.
- **Car I/O** (`selfdrive/pandad`, `selfdrive/car`) — talks to the comma "panda" CAN-bus interface hardware, decodes/encodes CAN into the car-agnostic `CarState`/`CarControl` message types via a per-brand interface defined in the vendored `opendbc_repo`.
- **System services** (`system/*`) — hardware abstraction, disk logging + cloud upload, remote SSH/telemetry access (athena), OTA updates, GPS daemons, and misc daemons (stats, time sync, crash reporting).
- **UI** (`selfdrive/ui`) — on-device touchscreen display (alerts, camera view, settings) and alert sounds.
- **Common** (`common/`) — shared library code used by literally every process above (params store, logging, rate-limiting, coordinate transforms, PID/Kalman primitives).

## 4. Entry Points

### 4.1 Device boot entry point: `launch_openpilot.sh` → `launch_chffrplus.sh`

Confirmed from `launch_openpilot.sh:1-3` (just `exec ./launch_chffrplus.sh`) and `launch_chffrplus.sh:1-88`.

```text
launch_openpilot.sh
  └─ exec launch_chffrplus.sh
       ├─ source launch_env.sh            # sets OMP/MKL/thread-count env vars, QCOM_PRIORITY, AGNOS_VERSION, STAGING_ROOT
       ├─ agnos_init()                     # only if /AGNOS exists (real device): sets boot-slot success flag (`abctl --set_success`),
       │                                   #   fixes /dev node permissions, and — if /VERSION != $AGNOS_VERSION — verifies and
       │                                   #   applies an AGNOS (base OS) update via system/hardware/tici/{agnos.py,updater}, or reboots
       ├─ launch():
       │    ├─ remove stale `.git/index.lock`
       │    ├─ overlay-update swap: if `.overlay_init` exists and the repo is unmodified since, and a
       │    │    finalized staged update exists at `${STAGING_ROOT}/finalized/.overlay_consistent`,
       │    │    atomically swap the current checkout for the staged one (`mv` old→backup, `mv` staged→live)
       │    │    and re-exec itself — this is the actual OTA "apply" step (produced by `system/updated`)
       │    ├─ symlink `/data/pythonpath` → cwd, export PYTHONPATH
       │    ├─ agnos_init (hardware-specific init) if `/AGNOS` marker file present
       │    ├─ `cd system/manager && ./build.py`  (compiles native code via SCons) — SKIPPED if a top-level `prebuilt` file exists (release images ship prebuilt binaries)
       │    └─ `./manager.py`                       — THE actual long-running entry point
       └─ (if manager.py ever returns) infinite `sleep 1` loop to keep a TTY error visible on-device
```

**Discrepancy note:** `launch_openpilot.sh` is the name suggested by the README's "Quick start" instructions, but it is a 2-line trampoline; the real logic — including the security-relevant OTA-apply step — lives in `launch_chffrplus.sh`, a name with no obvious connection to "openpilot" (legacy naming from comma's older "chffr"/"chffrplus" products). This isn't documented anywhere in the README.

### 4.2 Process-manager entry point: `system/manager/manager.py`

Confirmed from `system/manager/manager.py:183-236`.

```text
if __name__ == "__main__":
  unblock_stdout()
  main()
    ├─ manager_init()
    │    ├─ save_bootlog()
    │    ├─ get_build_metadata()                          # git commit/branch/origin/dirty flag, release-channel detection
    │    ├─ Params().clear_all(...)  × 4                    # clears params tagged CLEAR_ON_MANAGER_START / _ONROAD_TRANSITION /
    │    │                                                   #   _OFFROAD_TRANSITION / _IGNITION_ON, plus DEVELOPMENT_ONLY on release channels
    │    ├─ fill unset params with their registered default values
    │    ├─ mkdir shared-memory path (Paths.shm_path())
    │    ├─ write Version/GitCommit/GitCommitDate/GitBranch/GitRemote/IsTestedBranch/IsReleaseBranch/HardwareSerial params
    │    ├─ register(show_spinner=True)                     # obtains/validates the device's cloud "dongle ID"; raises if it fails
    │    ├─ export DONGLE_ID / GIT_ORIGIN / GIT_BRANCH / GIT_COMMIT env vars (consumed by swaglog)
    │    ├─ sentry.init(SELFDRIVE) + cloudlog.bind_global(...)   # crash reporting + structured logging context
    │    └─ p.prepare() for every managed process              # PythonProcess.prepare() = importlib.import_module(self.module) —
    │                                                            #   i.e. every enabled Python daemon's module is imported (but not run)
    │                                                            #   up front, inside the manager process, to catch import errors early
    │                                                            #   and warm Python's import cache before fork
    ├─ signal.signal(SIGTERM, → sys.exit(1))
    ├─ manager_thread()                                       # see below — runs until shutdown/reboot/uninstall requested
    │    (wrapped in try/except → sentry.capture_exception(); finally → manager_cleanup())
    └─ manager_cleanup()
         ├─ p.stop(block=False) for every process               # non-blocking SIGINT/SIGKILL to all
         └─ p.stop(block=True) for every process                # then block until all are confirmed dead
    then, back in main(): if DoUninstall/DoReboot/DoShutdown param is set, call the corresponding HARDWARE.* method.
```

`manager_thread()` (`system/manager/manager.py:107-180`) is the actual **supervisor loop**:

1. Builds an ignore-list of process names to never run: `manage_athenad`+`uploader` if the device has no registered dongle ID yet; `pandad` if `NOBOARD` env var set; anything listed in the `BLOCK` env var (comma-separated).
2. Opens a `SubMaster(['deviceState','carParams','pandaStates'], poll='deviceState')` and a `PubMaster(['managerState'])`.
3. `write_onroad_params(False, params)` then an initial `ensure_running(...)` call (offroad state) before entering the loop.
4. Loop forever, each iteration blocking on `sm.update(1000)` (i.e. driven by `deviceState` messages, ~1Hz, with a 1000ms timeout):
   - Reads `started = sm['deviceState'].started` (the offroad/onroad flag).
   - On offroad→onroad transition: clears `CLEAR_ON_ONROAD_TRANSITION` params. On onroad→offroad: clears `CLEAR_ON_OFFROAD_TRANSITION` params.
   - Computes `ignition` from any `pandaStates[].ignitionLine/ignitionCan` (excluding unknown panda types); on ignition-off→on edge, clears `CLEAR_ON_IGNITION_ON` params.
   - On any `started` transition, calls `write_onroad_params(started, params)` — this is what actually drives `pandad`'s safety-mode setter thread (per the code comment at `manager.py:144`).
   - Calls `ensure_running(managed_processes.values(), started, params, CP=sm['carParams'], not_run=ignore)` every iteration — this is the actual scheduler (see `system/manager/process.py` below).
   - Prints/logs a color-coded one-line status of every process (alive=green/dead=red).
   - Publishes a `managerState` message with per-process running/pid/exitcode state.
   - Touches `/var/tmp/power_watchdog` with the current monotonic time if all `deviceState` health checks pass (an external power-management watchdog reads this file — **inferred**, the consumer of this file is outside the scope explored).
   - Breaks the loop (leading to `manager_cleanup()` and process exit) if `DoUninstall`/`DoShutdown`/`DoReboot` params are set, recording `LastManagerExitReason`.

### 4.3 The process abstraction: `system/manager/process.py`

Three concrete `ManagerProcess` subclasses (confirmed `system/manager/process.py:62-247`):

| Class | Launch mechanism | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `PythonProcess` | `multiprocessing.Process(target=launcher, args=(module, name))` → `launcher()` does `importlib.import_module(proc)`, `setproctitle`, `messaging.reset_context()` (fresh SHM context post-fork), `cloudlog.bind(daemon=name)`, then calls `mod.main()` | Almost every daemon in this codebase — the vast majority of processes are plain Python modules each exposing a `main()` function |
| `NativeProcess` | `multiprocessing.Process(target=nativelauncher, ...)` → `nativelauncher()` does `os.chdir(cwd); os.execvp(pargs[0], pargs)` (replaces the forked Python process image entirely) | Compiled C++ daemons: `loggerd`, `encoderd`, `stream_encoderd`, `camerad`, `_pandad` (disabled), `bridge` |
| `DaemonProcess` | `subprocess.Popen(['python','-m',module], ..., preexec_fn=os.setpgrp)`, with its PID persisted to a `Params` key so it **survives manager restarts** (checked via `os.kill(pid, 0)` + reading `/proc/{pid}/cmdline`) | Only `manage_athenad` (`AthenadPid` param) — explicitly so an SSH/telemetry session isn't dropped when manager itself restarts |

`ensure_running()` (`process.py:249-267`) is the scheduler: for each registered process, if `enabled and name not in not_run and should_run(started, params, CP)`, ensure it's started (restarting it if `restart_if_crash` is set and it died); otherwise call `.stop(block=False)`. Every process's `should_run` is one of the small predicate functions defined at the top of `process_config.py` (`always_run`, `only_onroad`, `only_offroad`, `iscar`, `notcar`, `driverview`, `logging`, `ublox`, `joystick`/`not_joystick`, `long_maneuver`/`not_long_maneuver`, `qcomgps`), optionally combined with `and_()`/`or_()`.

| webjoystick (debug) | Python | `tools.bodyteleop.web` | `notcar` | Web-based joystick UI |
| joystick (debug) | Python | `tools.joystick.joystick_control` | `joystick` AND `iscar` | Interactive joystick control |

Key `should_run` predicates, all `system/manager/process_config.py:12-56`: `driverview` = started OR `IsDriverViewEnabled` param; `notcar`/`iscar` gate on `CarParams.notCar` (true for sim/bench "cars"); `logging` = onroad AND (car requires it OR `DisableLogging` not set); `ublox` = presence of `/dev/ttyHS0` AND absence of `/persist/comma/use-quectel-gps` marker file (also persists this as the `UbloxAvailable` param); `joystick`/`long_maneuver` gate on debug params `JoystickDebugMode`/`LongitudinalManeuverMode`.

## Car Interface Layer

### Overview and pipeline position

This section covers the boundary between the physical CAN bus / comma "panda" hardware and the rest of openpilot's control stack: `selfdrive/pandad/` (the process that talks to the panda over USB/SPI) and `selfdrive/car/` (the "card" process and its helpers, which turn raw CAN frames into the brand-agnostic `CarState`/`CarControl`/`CarParams` structs consumed by `selfdrived`/`controlsd`/`plannerd`).

Data flow (confirmed from code):

```
panda MCU (firmware, enforces safety) <--USB/SPI-->
  selfdrive/pandad/pandad.cc (C++ process "pandad")
    publishes: can (100Hz), pandaStates (10Hz), peripheralState (2Hz)
    subscribes: sendcan, selfdriveState, deviceState, driverCameraState
      |
      v  cereal "can" socket
  selfdrive/car/card.py (Python process "card")
    subscribes: can (drives loop), pandaStates, carControl, onroadEvents
    publishes: sendcan, carState, carParams, carOutput, liveTracks
      |
      v  cereal "carState" socket
  selfdrived / controlsd / plannerd (out of scope here)
      |
      v  cereal "carControl" socket (consumed by card.py's controls_update)
```

`pandad` is a dumb, brand-agnostic transport: it moves raw CAN frames between the panda and the `can`/`sendcan` cereal sockets and mirrors `CarParams.safetyConfigs`/`alternativeExperience` into the panda's firmware-enforced safety mode once `card` has finished fingerprinting. It has no knowledge of `CarInterface`, DBC files, or per-brand logic. `card` owns the `CarInterfaceBase` instance (`selfdrive/car/card.py:60-152`), decodes CAN into `CarState`, and encodes `CarControl` into outgoing CAN messages (`selfdrive/car/card.py:223-239`).

Process registration (confirmed): `system/manager/process_config.py:92` registers `card` as `PythonProcess("card", "selfdrive.car.card", only_onroad)`; `system/manager/process_config.py:96` registers `pandad` as `PythonProcess("pandad", "selfdrive.pandad.pandad", always_run)`; `system/manager/process_config.py:86` registers the native `_pandad` binary (`enabled=False`, launched indirectly by the Python `pandad` wrapper via `subprocess.Popen`, see below).

Cereal service rates relevant to this layer (confirmed from `cereal/services.py:33-66`): `can` 100 Hz, `sendcan` 100 Hz, `carState`/`carControl`/`carOutput` 100 Hz, `pandaStates` 10 Hz, `liveTracks` 20 Hz, `onroadEvents` 1 Hz, `carParams` 0.02 Hz (i.e. once per 50s).

---

## `selfdrive/pandad/` — the pandad process

### Purpose

`pandad` is a two-stage process: a Python wrapper (`pandad.py`) that discovers, flashes, and health-checks connected panda(s) over USB, then execs a native C++ binary (`pandad.cc`/`main.cc`) that runs the actual realtime CAN I/O loop and forwards the panda's firmware-reported safety/health telemetry into cereal.

### `selfdrive/pandad/pandad.py` (Python wrapper)

| Function | Signature | Purpose | Side effects |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flash_f4_panda` | `(panda: Panda) -> None` | Re-flashes legacy/deprecated F4 pandas (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.py:18-39`) | Writes firmware over USB via `Panda.flash_static` |
| `get_expected_signature` | `() -> bytes` | Reads the expected H7 firmware signature from `FW_PATH` (`:41-47`) | Reads file; swallows/logs exceptions, returns `b""` on error |
| `flash_panda` | `(panda_serial: str) -> Panda` | Connects to one panda, flashes if signature mismatches or in bootstub, recovers if still stuck (`:49-96`) | USB flash, `panda.recover()`, raises `AssertionError` if panda never boots or version mismatches persist |
| `check_panda_support` | `(panda) -> bool` | Checks `panda.get_type()` against `Panda.SUPPORTED_DEVICES` (`:98-103`) | none |
| `main` | `() -> None` | Outer supervisor loop (`:105-221`) | see below |

`main()` loop (confirmed, `:105-221`): registers a `SIGINT` handler that sets `do_exit` and forwards the signal to the child `pandad` process; loops until `do_exit`:
1. Clears `PandaSignatures` param.
2. If no panda was found last iteration (`no_internal_panda_count`), resets or (after 3 misses) DFU-recovers the internal panda via `HARDWARE.recover_internal_panda()`/`reset_internal_panda()`.
3. Recovers any pandas already sitting in DFU mode (`PandaDFU.list()` / `.recover()`).
4. Lists all connected panda serials (`Panda.list()`); if none found, increments the miss counter and `continue`s.
5. Flashes every found panda (`flash_panda`), confirms the internal panda is present if the hardware expects one, sorts pandas deterministically (internal first, then type, then serial), writes `PandaSignatures` param, resets each panda on `first_run`, checks health for `heartbeat_lost`/`som_reset_triggered` and records params/cloudlog events, then closes each `Panda` USB handle.
6. Broad `except` clauses catch `usb1.USBErrorNoDevice`/`USBErrorPipe` (panda disconnected mid-setup) and any other `Exception` (logged via `cloudlog.exception("pandad.uncaught_exception")`) — both simply `continue` the outer loop, i.e. **any unexpected exception here is swallowed and retried**, not fatal.
7. Once flashing/health-check succeeds, spawns the native binary: `subprocess.Popen(["./pandad", *panda_serials], cwd=.../selfdrive/pandad)` and blocks on `process.wait()`. When that process exits (crash, or `SIGINT` forwarded from step-1 handler), the outer `while` loop iterates again — i.e. the Python wrapper **restarts the native pandad indefinitely** any time it exits, until `do_exit`.

This is the only place firmware flashing happens; the native process assumes up-to-date firmware and raises (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.cc:74-79`, see below) if a mismatch is detected, which is a fatal crash of the native process (caught nowhere in C++) — causing the Python wrapper to relaunch it, but note flashing already happened before `Popen`, so this is a safety net for firmware installed after the wrapper's own check, not the normal path.

### `selfdrive/pandad/main.cc` — native process entry point

`main()` (`selfdrive/pandad/main.cc:8-22`): on-device (`!Hardware::PC()`) sets realtime priority 54 and pins to CPU core 3 (`util::set_realtime_priority(54)`, `util::set_core_affinity({3})`, both asserted to succeed). Collects `argv[1:]` as the list of panda serials and calls `pandad_main_thread(serials)`.

### `selfdrive/pandad/pandad.cc` — connection and main loop

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `check_all_connected(pandas)` (`:46-54`) | Returns false and sets global `do_exit=true` if any `Panda::connected()` is false |
| `connect(serial, index)` (`:56-82`) | Constructs a `Panda` at CAN bus offset `index*PANDA_BUS_OFFSET` (4 buses per panda, `:26` in `pandad.h`), configures loopback (env `BOARDD_LOOPBACK`) and CAN-FD auto-detect on all 3 CAN channels; **raises `std::runtime_error` if firmware is out of date** (unless `BOARDD_SKIP_FW_CHECK` env is set or the device is unsupported/BLACK_PANDA) |
| `can_send_thread(pandas, fake_send)` (`:84-114`) | Dedicated thread subscribing to `sendcan`; forwards each received CAN frame batch to every connected panda via `panda->can_send()`, unless the message is >1s old (`nanos_since_boot() - logMonoTime >= 1e9`) or `fake_send` (env `FAKESEND`) is set, in which case it's dropped and logged as an error |
| `can_recv(pandas, pm)` (`:116-136`) | Polls `can_receive()` on every panda into a shared static buffer, publishes one `can` message per main-loop iteration; message `valid` is false if any panda's `can_receive` reports unhealthy comms |
| `fill_panda_state` / `fill_panda_can_state` (`:138-192`) | Copy the raw `health_t`/`can_health_t` C structs from the panda's firmware into the `PandaState`/`PandaCanState` capnp builders (voltage, uptime, fault bits, safety mode/param, bus-off counters, etc.) |
| `send_panda_states(pm, pandas, is_onroad, spoofing_started)` (`:194-295`) | Builds and publishes `pandaStates`; also **acts on health data**: forces `NO_OUTPUT` safety if firmware unexpectedly reports `SILENT`, toggles power-saving based on ignition, and — critically — **forces `SafetyModel::NO_OUTPUT` whenever ignition is off or the device is not onroad** (`:261-265`), independent of whatever `card`/`CarParams` requested. Returns `std::nullopt` if any panda's health read fails (signals caller to bail); otherwise returns whether ignition is present on any panda |
| `send_peripheral_state` (`:297-328`) | Publishes `peripheralState` (voltage/current/fan speed) at the caller's cadence |
| `process_panda_state` (`:330-370`) | Wraps `send_panda_states`, decides whether to trigger a reconnect (`do_exit=true`) if ignition is off and comms are unhealthy, or if a new panda serial appears that isn't in the currently-connected set; sends the heartbeat (`engaged` flag) to every panda every call |
| `process_peripheral_state` (`:372-434`) | Fan-speed control from `deviceState.fanSpeedPercentDesired`; IR LED power control from driver-camera `integLines`, filtered through `FirstOrderFilter`s (different time constants for normal vs. driver-view), with a 1s input timeout that forces IR off |
| `pandad_run(pandas)` (`:436-502`) | Main loop, see below |
| `pandad_main_thread(serials)` (`:504-542`) | Entry point called from `main()`. If no serials were passed as argv, calls `Panda::list()` to auto-discover; retries `connect()` per serial every 100ms until success or `do_exit`; once all pandas are connected, calls `pandad_run`; on exit, `delete`s every `Panda*` |

`pandad_run` main loop (confirmed, `:436-502`), driven by `RateKeeper rk("pandad", 100)` (100 Hz target, and — unlike `card.py` — **this loop does call `rk.keepTime()`**, i.e. it actively paces itself, not merely monitors lag):
- Every iteration: `can_recv(pandas, &pm)` — publish `can` (100 Hz).
- Every 5th iteration (20 Hz): `process_peripheral_state`.
- Every 10th iteration (10 Hz): `sm.update(0)` on `selfdriveState`; compute `engaged` (`allAliveAndValid && selfdriveState.enabled`) and `is_onroad` (`Params().getBool("IsOnroad")`); call `process_panda_state` (publishes `pandaStates`, sends heartbeat) and `panda_safety.configureSafetyMode(is_onroad)` (see `PandaSafety` below — this is where `CarParams` gets pushed into panda firmware).
- Every 50th iteration (2 Hz): `send_peripheral_state`.
- Every iteration: drains each panda's UART serial log buffer and forwards it to `cloudlog` (`LOGE` if the string contains `"Register 0x"`, else `LOGD`).
- Loop exits when `do_exit` or a panda disconnects (`check_all_connected`).
- On exit, if the device was onroad and not engaged, force every connected panda to `SafetyModel::NO_OUTPUT` before returning (closes the relay defensively) — a second, redundant relay-close mechanism alongside `send_panda_states`'s per-frame enforcement.
- `send_thread.join()` on exit.

Concurrency (confirmed): the native `pandad` is **two-threaded** — the main thread (recv + state publish, realtime priority) and a dedicated `can_send_thread` (subscribes `sendcan`, blocking receive with 100ms timeout, forwards to all pandas). No other threads. Shared state between the threads is limited to the `pandas` vector of `Panda*` (each `Panda` object internally serializes USB/SPI I/O; no explicit mutex is visible in these files, so thread-safety relies on the underlying `PandaCommsHandle`/USB layer, not proven safe from this file alone — **uncertain**, would need `panda_comms.cc` review to fully confirm).

### `PandaSafety` (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.h:11-27`, `panda_safety.cc`)

This class is the concrete code path by which the Python-computed `CarParams.safetyConfigs` get pushed into the panda's firmware-enforced safety model — i.e., the Python/C++ boundary that hands control to the hardware safety layer.

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `configureSafetyMode(bool is_onroad)` (`panda_safety.cc:5-20`) | Entry point, called every 10th main-loop iteration. If onroad and not yet configured: calls `updateMultiplexingMode()`, then `fetchCarParams()`; if non-empty, calls `setSafetyMode()` and latches `safety_configured_ = true` (so it configures **once** per onroad session, not every 10 frames). If not onroad, resets all three latches (`initialized_`, `safety_configured_`, `log_once_`) so it reconfigures fresh next time onroad goes true. |
| `updateMultiplexingMode()` (`:22-42`) | On first-ever call, sets every panda to `SafetyModel::ELM327` with `safety_param=1` (no OBD multiplexing) to allow initial fingerprinting reads. Thereafter, watches the `ObdMultiplexingEnabled` param (set by `card.py`'s `obd_callback`, see below) and re-applies `ELM327` mode with `safety_param` toggled between pandas (panda 0 gets `0` i.e. multiplexing-enabled only if requested and it's the first panda; all others always get `1`) whenever the param value changes, then writes `ObdMultiplexingChanged=true` to unblock the Python side which polls that param. |
| `fetchCarParams()` (`:44-58`) | Returns `""` (no-op) until `Params.FirmwareQueryDone` is true (set by `card.py` once `get_car()` fingerprinting completes) **and** `Params.ControlsReady` is true (set by `card.py` once `CarInterface.init()` has run). Only then returns the raw serialized `CarParams` bytes from the `CarParams` param. |
| `setSafetyMode(params_string)` (`:60-81`) | Deserializes the `CarParams` capnp bytes, reads `safetyConfigs` (list, index-aligned with `pandas_`) and `alternativeExperience`. For each panda, if there's a corresponding `SafetyConfig` entry, applies its `safetyModel`/`safetyParam`; **pandas beyond the length of `safetyConfigs` default to `SafetyModel::SILENT`** (per the "Multi-panda conventions" comment at `pandad.cc:33-36`). Calls `panda->set_alternative_experience()` and `panda->set_safety_model()`, which are USB/SPI control transfers into panda firmware. |

Security-relevant note (confirmed): the **panda firmware itself** is the actual safety boundary (bounds-checks steering/gas/brake commands, enforces the configured `SafetyModel`). All of this Python/C++ code only *selects which safety model and parameters* the firmware will enforce; it does not implement torque/accel limiting itself. Until `configureSafetyMode` completes its first successful `setSafetyMode` call, pandas remain in `ELM327` (an inert/diagnostic mode with `safety_param` gating OBD multiplexing) — meaning no car-specific actuation is possible before `card` has fingerprinted the car and initialized the interface. Additionally, regardless of `CarParams`, `send_panda_states` forces `NO_OUTPUT` whenever ignition is off or not onroad, independent of and prior to whatever `PandaSafety` last configured — a second, independent gate.

### CAN message shuttling: `can_capnp_to_list` / `can_list_to_can_capnp`

Defined in `selfdrive/pandad/pandad_api_impl.py` (imported into `selfdrive/pandad/__init__.py:1` for use as `openpilot.selfdrive.pandad.can_capnp_to_list`/`can_list_to_can_capnp`, and used directly by `selfdrive/car/card.py:20`).

| Function | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `can_list_to_can_capnp` | `(can_msgs, msgtype='can', valid=True) -> bytes` (`:29-57`) | Builds a `log.Event` capnp message with `logMonoTime=time.monotonic()*1e9`, populates a `List(CanData)` field named `msgtype` (`"can"` or `"sendcan"`) from `(address, dat, src)` tuples, and serializes to bytes. Caches the capnp schema `Field` objects for `address`/`dat`/`src` in module-level globals (`_cached_writer_fields`) on first call as a micro-optimization to skip repeated string-based field lookups. |
| `can_capnp_to_list` | `(strings, msgtype='can') -> list[tuple[int, list[tuple]]]` (`:60-88`) | Inverse: for each serialized bytes blob, decodes the `log.Event` (with `traversal_limit_in_words=NO_TRAVERSAL_LIMIT`, i.e. unbounded — trusts the input size), extracts `logMonoTime` and the list of `(address, dat, src)` tuples from the named field. Same reader-field caching strategy. |

Both functions use the **same global cache for all calls in the process** — this is safe only because the `CanData` schema (`address`/`dat`/`src` fields) is identical regardless of `msgtype` (`"can"` vs `"sendcan"`); the cache is not keyed by msgtype (confirmed from code — a latent fragility if the schemas ever diverged, but currently correct).

---

## `selfdrive/car/card.py` — the "card" process

### Purpose

`card` is the single Python process that: (1) owns fingerprinting/instantiation of the brand-specific `CarInterfaceBase`, (2) every CAN-driven cycle decodes CAN → `CarState` and publishes it, (3) on each `carControl` update, encodes it to CAN via the interface's `CarController` and publishes `sendcan`, and (4) manages a few persistent Params (`CarParams`, `ControlsReady`, `IsMetric`, etc.) that other processes and `pandad`'s `PandaSafety` depend on.

Sockets (confirmed, `Car.__init__`, `card.py:66-68`):
- `can_sock = messaging.sub_sock('can', timeout=20)` — raw subscriber (not via `SubMaster`), 20ms timeout, drained manually.
- `sm = messaging.SubMaster(['pandaStates', 'carControl', 'onroadEvents'])`.
- `pm = messaging.PubMaster(['sendcan', 'carState', 'carParams', 'carOutput', 'liveTracks'])`.

### Module-level helpers

| Function | Signature | Purpose | Callers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `obd_callback` | `(params: Params) -> ObdCallback` (`:31-39`) | Returns a closure `set_obd_multiplexing(bool)` that, on change, clears `ObdMultiplexingChanged`, writes `ObdMultiplexingEnabled`, then **blocks** (`params.get_bool("ObdMultiplexingChanged", block=True)`) until `pandad`'s `PandaSafety.updateMultiplexingMode()` acknowledges by setting that param — i.e. a synchronous Python↔C++ handshake over Params. | Passed into `get_car()` as the `set_obd_multiplexing` argument, used during fingerprinting (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/car_helpers.py:103,122`) and can be re-passed to `CarInterface.init/deinit` (e.g. Toyota's radar-disable path) |
| `can_comm_callbacks` | `(logcan, sendcan) -> (CanRecvCallable, CanSendCallable)` (`:42-57`) | Builds the `can_recv`/`can_send` closures passed to `get_car()` and stored as `self.can_callbacks`, used again later for `CI.init()`/`CI.deinit()`. `can_recv(wait_for_one=False)` drains `logcan` (optionally blocking for one message) and returns `list[list[CanData]]` (one list per received capnp `Event`). `can_send(msgs)` serializes and publishes to `sendcan`. | `Car.__init__`, `Car.controls_update` |

### Class `Car` (`card.py:60-270`)

The entire process state lives in one `Car` instance; there is exactly one instantiated per process (`main()`).

**Class-level annotations** (`:61-63`): `CI: CarInterfaceBase`, `RI: RadarInterfaceBase`, `CP: car.CarParams` — documents the three "identity" objects but they're actually assigned in `__init__`.

**`__init__(self, CI=None, RI=None)`** (`:65-157`) — constructor and effectively the whole fingerprinting/setup sequence:
1. Opens sockets/pub-sub as above; `can_rcv_cum_timeout_counter = 0`; `CC_prev`/`CS_prev` initialized to empty `CarControl`/`CarState` capnp messages; `initialized_prev = False`; `last_actuators_output = structs.CarControl.Actuators()` (opendbc struct, not capnp).
2. `self.params = Params()`; builds `can_callbacks` via `can_comm_callbacks`.
3. Reads `IsReleaseBranch` param → `is_release`.
4. **If `CI` is not injected** (normal runtime path, `CI=None` — test/replay code can inject a pre-built `CI`/`RI` to skip fingerprinting):
   - Blocks with a `print` + `messaging.recv_one_retry(self.can_sock)` loop until at least one non-empty CAN packet is seen.
   - Reads `AlphaLongitudinalEnabled` param.
   - Attempts to load a cached `CarParams` from the `CarParamsCache` param (deserializes via `car.CarParams.from_bytes`) to skip re-fingerprinting (used by `opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/car_helpers.py:93-98` inside `fingerprint()`).
   - Calls `get_car(*self.can_callbacks, obd_callback(self.params), alpha_long_allowed, is_release, cached_params)` (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/car_helpers.py:151-166`) — this performs VIN/FW-based and CAN-based fingerprinting and returns an instantiated `CarInterface`.
   - Instantiates the brand's `RadarInterface` via `interfaces[self.CI.CP.carFingerprint].RadarInterface(self.CI.CP)`.
   - `self.CP = self.CI.CP`.
   - Writes `FirmwareQueryDone=True` — this is the param `pandad`'s `PandaSafety.fetchCarParams()` polls for (see above) to know fingerprinting is complete.
5. **Else** (`CI` injected): `self.CI, self.CP = CI, CI.CP`; `self.RI = RI`. (Used by tests / process-replay harnesses.)
6. `self.CP.alternativeExperience = 0` (hardcoded reset — always 0 regardless of what the brand's `_get_params` set, worth flagging: this line unconditionally overwrites whatever the interface may have configured for `alternativeExperience` before it's ever used downstream, meaning per-car alternative-experience panda flags set by `_get_params` are always discarded here — **confirmed from code**, likely intentional since this field is meant to be user/toggle driven rather than car-specific, but there is no comment explaining it).
7. Computes `controller_available = self.CI.CC is not None and OpenpilotEnabledToggle and not self.CP.dashcamOnly`; sets `self.CP.passive = not controller_available or self.CP.dashcamOnly`. If passive, **forces `safetyConfigs` to a single `noOutput` entry** — i.e. passive mode is enforced both at the Python level (no `controls_update` calls) and by telling the panda firmware to refuse all output.
8. SecOC key handling (`:119-138`, Toyota/SecOC-required cars only): tries to copy a user-provided key from `/cache/params/SecOCKey` into the `SecOCKey` param (best-effort, bare `except: pass`); if a 16-byte key is present, sets `CP.secOcKeyAvailable = True` and copies the key onto `self.CI.CS.secoc_key` and (if controller available) `self.CI.CC.secoc_key`. Logs a warning if the stored key has the wrong length.
9. Rotates `CarParamsPersistent` → `CarParamsPrevRoute` (best-effort route history), then writes the now-finalized `CP` to `CarParams` (blocking `put`), `CarParamsCache` and `CarParamsPersistent` (both `put_nonblocking`). **This `CarParams` param write is exactly what `PandaSafety.fetchCarParams()` reads on the C++ side** once `ControlsReady` also becomes true.
10. `self.v_cruise_helper = VCruiseHelper(self.CP)` (see `cruise.py` below).
11. Reads `IsMetric`/`ExperimentalMode` params into `self.is_metric`/`self.experimental_mode`.
12. `self.rk = Ratekeeper(100, print_delay_threshold=None)` — comment: *"card is driven by can recv, expected at 100Hz"*.

**`state_update(self) -> tuple[car.CarState, structs.RadarDataT | None]`** (`:159-191`) — "carState update loop, driven by can":
1. `can_strs = messaging.drain_sock_raw(self.can_sock, wait_for_one=True)` — **this is the blocking call that paces the whole process**; it waits for at least one `can` message (subject to the socket's 20ms timeout set in `__init__`).
2. Decodes via `can_capnp_to_list`.
3. `CS = self.CI.update(can_list)` — brand-specific CAN→CarState decode (see `CarInterfaceBase.update`, below).
4. `RD = self.RI.update(can_list)` — radar decode (may be `None` most frames; base implementation returns non-`None` only every 5th call, i.e. 20 Hz — see `RadarInterfaceBase.update`).
5. `self.sm.update(0)` — non-blocking poll of `pandaStates`/`carControl`/`onroadEvents`.
6. `can_rcv_valid = len(can_strs) > 0`; if not valid, increments `self.can_rcv_cum_timeout_counter` (this cumulative counter, never reset, is published every frame as `carState.canErrorCounter`).
7. If `REPLAY` env var is set and CAN was valid, latches `self.can_log_mono_time` from the first CAN event's `logMonoTime` (used later in `controls_update` to keep `sendcan` timestamps consistent with the replayed log instead of wall-clock, so `can_send_thread`'s 1-second staleness check in `pandad.cc` doesn't discard replayed sends).
8. Calls `self.v_cruise_helper.update_v_cruise(CS, self.sm['carControl'].enabled, self.is_metric)`.
9. If `carControl.enabled` just became true this frame (rising edge vs `self.CC_prev.enabled`), calls `self.v_cruise_helper.initialize_v_cruise(self.CS_prev, self.experimental_mode)` — uses **last frame's** `CarState` (buttons that caused the enable) rather than the current one; comment: *"Use CarState w/ buttons from the step selfdrived enables on"*.
10. Copies `v_cruise_kph`/`v_cruise_cluster_kph` from the helper onto `CS.vCruise`/`CS.vCruiseCluster` (marked with a `# TODO: mirror the carState.cruiseState struct?` comment — i.e. the author considers this plumbing not fully clean/final).
11. Returns `(CS, RD)`.

**`state_publish(self, CS, RD)`** (`:193-221`) — "carState and carParams publish loop":
- Publishes `carParams` only every `50/DT_CTRL = 5000` frames (`sm.frame % 5000 == 0`, i.e. every 50s at 100Hz) — matches the `carParams` service rate of 0.02 Hz declared in `cereal/services.py`. Comment: "logged every 50 seconds (> 1 per segment)".
- Publishes `carOutput` every frame; `valid = sm.all_checks(['carControl'])`; payload is `self.last_actuators_output` — i.e. **this publishes the previous frame's actuator output** (updated only inside `controls_update`, which runs after `state_publish` in `step()` — see the loop ordering note below), not something computed this frame. Comment: *"kick off controlsd step while we actuate the latest carControl packet"* — the intent is to unblock the downstream `controlsd`/`selfdrived` step as early as possible in the frame.
- Publishes `carState`; `valid = CS.canValid`; also stamps `carState.canErrorCounter = self.can_rcv_cum_timeout_counter` and `carState.cumLagMs = -self.rk.remaining * 1000.` here (i.e. `cumLagMs` reflects `Ratekeeper`'s notion of schedule drift even though the loop is not actually rate-limited by `Ratekeeper`, only monitored by it — see `card_thread` below).
- Publishes `liveTracks` only if `RD is not None`; `valid = not any(RD.errors.to_dict().values())`.

**`controls_update(self, CS, CC)`** (`:223-239`) — "control update loop, driven by carControl":
- On the **first** call after `initialized_prev` was `False` (i.e. exactly once, right after `selfdrived` finishes initializing — see `step()`), calls `self.CI.init(self.CP, *self.can_callbacks)` (brand-specific ECU knockout/setup, e.g. Toyota's radar-disable UDS call) and writes `ControlsReady=True` (nonblocking) — **this is the param `pandad`'s `PandaSafety.fetchCarParams()` waits on** as the second half of the gate before pushing `CarParams` into panda firmware safety mode. Code comment flags a known limitation: *"this can make us miss at least a few cycles when doing an ECU knockout"*.
- If `carControl` is alive (`sm.all_alive(['carControl'])`): computes `now_nanos` (replayed timestamp if `REPLAY`, else `time.monotonic()*1e9`), calls `self.last_actuators_output, can_sends = self.CI.apply(CC, now_nanos)` (brand `CarController.update`), and publishes `sendcan` via `can_list_to_can_capnp(can_sends, msgtype='sendcan', valid=CS.canValid)` — **note `sendcan`'s validity is tied to whether the *current* CAN read was valid**, not to `carControl`'s own validity. Updates `self.CC_prev = CC`.
- If `carControl` is *not* alive, this method silently does nothing (no `sendcan` published that frame) beyond the possible `CI.init()` call above.

**`step(self)`** (`:241-252`) — one full iteration, called every loop:
1. `CS, RD = self.state_update()`.
2. `self.state_publish(CS, RD)`.
3. Computes `initialized`: true iff no active `onroadEvents` entry named `selfdriveInitializing` **and** `onroadEvents` has been seen at least once (`sm.seen['onroadEvents']`).
4. If not passive and `initialized`: `self.controls_update(CS, self.sm['carControl'])`.
5. `self.initialized_prev = initialized`; `self.CS_prev = CS`.

Ordering note (confirmed): `state_publish` (which reads `self.last_actuators_output`) runs **before** `controls_update` (which writes it) in each `step()` — so the `carOutput` published in frame *N* reflects the actuator command computed in frame *N-1*, a deliberate one-frame lag per the comment in `state_publish`.

**`params_thread(self, evt)`** (`:254-258`) — background thread body: while `evt` not set, re-reads `IsMetric` and `ExperimentalMode` (gated by `CP.openpilotLongitudinalControl`) into `self.is_metric`/`self.experimental_mode` every 100ms. This is the **only** cross-thread mutable state in the process — `is_metric`/`experimental_mode` are written by this thread and read by the main loop (`state_update`) without any lock. Since both are simple attribute assignments/reads of primitive `bool`s in CPython (GIL-protected), this is benign in practice but is not formally synchronized — flagged as a soft concurrency note, not a bug.

**`card_thread(self)`** (`:260-270`) — starts `params_thread` as a daemon-like (not literally daemon, but `join()`ed in `finally`) background `threading.Thread`, then loops `while True: self.step(); self.rk.monitor_time()` forever. On any exception escaping the loop (none are caught here), the `finally` block sets the stop event and joins the thread before the exception propagates — i.e. **`card_thread` itself does not catch exceptions from `step()`**; an unhandled exception in `CI.update`/`CI.apply`/etc. will crash the whole `card` process (which `system/manager` would then be responsible for restarting, per its own supervision policy — out of scope here). There is no per-iteration try/except around `step()`.

Important nuance: **`self.rk.monitor_time()` is called, not `self.rk.keep_time()`** (`common/realtime.py:72-96`). `monitor_time()` only tracks lag statistics (updates `_frame`, `_remaining`, `avg_dt`) — it does **not** sleep. So `Ratekeeper` here is used purely for **lag measurement** (feeding `cumLagMs` into published `carState`), not for actually pacing the loop; the loop's true cadence is governed entirely by how fast `messaging.drain_sock_raw(..., wait_for_one=True)` returns, i.e. by the rate of incoming `can` messages from `pandad` (nominally 100 Hz, matching the `can` service rate). This is a discrepancy worth calling out: the docstring/comment "card is driven by can recv, expected at 100Hz" is accurate, but a reader might assume `Ratekeeper(100, ...)` here enforces 100 Hz the way it does in most other openpilot processes — it does not; it only monitors it, since `keep_time()` is never called.

**`main()`** (`:273-276`): `config_realtime_process(4, Priority.CTRL_HIGH)` (pins to CPU core 4, realtime priority 53 — see `common/realtime.py:20-41`), instantiates `Car()` (runs the full fingerprinting `__init__` synchronously), then calls `car.card_thread()` (never returns under normal operation).

### Error handling / fallback behavior summary (card.py)

| Condition | Handling |
|---|---|
| No CAN packets within socket timeout | `can_rcv_valid=False`; `can_rcv_cum_timeout_counter` incremented; `carState.canValid` still reflects `CI.update`'s own `canValid` computation (from `CANParser.can_valid`/checksums), not directly this counter |
| Fingerprint fails to match any known car | `opendbc/car/car_helpers.py:get_car` falls back to `candidate = "MOCK"` (confirmed, `car_helpers.py:155-157`) rather than raising |
| SecOC key file missing/unreadable | Bare `except Exception: pass` (`card.py:126-127`) — silently ignored, falls through to checking the `SecOCKey` param instead |
| SecOC key present but wrong length | Logged via `cloudlog.warning`, `secOcKeyAvailable` left `False` |
| Exception inside `step()` | Not caught anywhere in `card.py`; propagates out of `card_thread()`, process crashes (background `params_thread` is still joined via `finally` first) |
| `carControl` not alive | `controls_update` skips sending `sendcan` for that frame; no exception |
| Car interface not "controller_available" (toggle off / dashcam-only / no `CC`) | `CP.passive=True`, forced `noOutput` safety config, `controls_update` never invoked from `step()` |

### Concurrency summary (card.py)

Single main thread running `step()` in a tight (CAN-recv-blocked, not `sleep`-paced) loop, plus one lightweight background thread (`params_thread`) that only touches two `bool` attributes. No explicit locks; no subprocesses spawned from this file. Compare with `pandad`'s native process, which has two real worker threads (recv/state vs. `sendcan` forwarding).

## `selfdrive/car/cruise.py` — `VCruiseHelper`

### Purpose

Implements openpilot's own cruise-set-speed state machine for cars where `CarParams.pcmCruise` is `False` (i.e. the car's stock ACC doesn't own the set speed — openpilot must track and adjust it itself from steering-wheel button presses), and mirrors the PCM's own set speed when `pcmCruise` is `True`. Runs entirely inside `Car.state_update()` (`card.py:182-189`).

### Module constants (`cruise.py:11-28`)

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `V_CRUISE_MIN` | 8 (kph) | Floor for openpilot-managed set speed |
| `V_CRUISE_MAX` | 145 (kph) | Ceiling; comment warns this is based on the model's training distribution — "model predictions above this speed can be unpredictable" |
| `V_CRUISE_UNSET` | 255 | Sentinel meaning "no set speed yet" |
| `V_CRUISE_INITIAL` | 40 (kph) | Default speed when enabling in normal mode with no better estimate |
| `V_CRUISE_INITIAL_EXPERIMENTAL_MODE` | 105 (kph) | Default speed when enabling in Experimental Mode |
| `IMPERIAL_INCREMENT` | `round(CV.MPH_TO_KPH, 1)` | Per-press increment size in imperial-unit mode |
| `CRUISE_LONG_PRESS` | 50 (frames, i.e. 0.5s at 100Hz) | Threshold to distinguish a long button hold from a tap |
| `CRUISE_NEAREST_FUNC` | `{accelCruise: ceil, decelCruise: floor}` | Used to snap to the nearest 5-unit boundary on long-press |
| `CRUISE_INTERVAL_SIGN` | `{accelCruise: +1, decelCruise: -1}` | Direction of adjustment |

### Class `VCruiseHelper`

**`__init__(self, CP)`** (`:32-38`): stores `CP`; `v_cruise_kph = v_cruise_cluster_kph = V_CRUISE_UNSET`; `v_cruise_kph_last = 0`; per-button press-duration timers (`button_timers`) and per-button "state at time of press" snapshots (`button_change_states`, tracking `standstill`/`enabled` at press time) for `decelCruise`/`accelCruise` only.

**`v_cruise_initialized` (property)** (`:40-42`): `v_cruise_kph != V_CRUISE_UNSET`.

**`update_v_cruise(self, CS, enabled, is_metric)`** (`:44-64`) — called every frame from `card.py:182`:
- `v_cruise_kph_last = v_cruise_kph` (snapshot before mutating).
- If `CS.cruiseState.available`:
  - If `not CP.pcmCruise`: delegates to `_update_v_cruise_non_pcm` (button-driven logic), mirrors the result into `v_cruise_cluster_kph`, and calls `update_button_timers`.
  - Else (PCM owns cruise): reads `CS.cruiseState.speed`/`speedCluster` directly (converted `MS_TO_KPH`); special-cases `speed==0` → both set to `V_CRUISE_UNSET`, and `speed==-1` → both set to `-1` (sentinel passthrough for cars that report "no valid speed" as -1, e.g. some PCM systems mid-transition).
- Else (`cruiseState.available` is false): both set to `V_CRUISE_UNSET`.

**`_update_v_cruise_non_pcm(self, CS, enabled, is_metric)`** (`:66-112`) — button-press state machine, only reached when `not CP.pcmCruise`:
- No-op if `not enabled`.
- Scans `CS.buttonEvents` for a **release** (`not b.pressed`) of `accelCruise`/`decelCruise`: if found and the corresponding timer exceeds `CRUISE_LONG_PRESS`, treats it as "end of long press" and returns without adjusting (the long-press adjustment already happened incrementally — see next bullet); otherwise records `button_type` for a short-press adjustment.
- If no release event was found this frame, falls back to checking `button_timers` for a button whose timer is a nonzero multiple of `CRUISE_LONG_PRESS` (i.e. still held down and just crossed another 0.5s boundary) → sets `long_press=True` and `button_type` accordingly. This is how long-press produces **repeated** increments every 0.5s while held, versus a single increment on release for a short tap.
- If no `button_type` resolved at all, returns (nothing to do).
- Standstill guard: if the button was pressed while standstill (per `button_change_states[...]["standstill"]`) or currently standstill, and it's `accelCruise`, returns — don't adjust speed just because resume was used to exit standstill.
- Rising-edge guard: if `enabled` was false at the moment this button was pressed (per `button_change_states[...]["enabled"]`), returns — comment: "Don't adjust speed if we've enabled since the button was depressed (some ports enable on rising edge)".
- Computes `v_cruise_delta` (1 kph metric or `IMPERIAL_INCREMENT`), multiplied by 5 if `long_press`.
- On a long press landing on a non-multiple of the delta (partial interval), **snaps** to the nearest boundary via `CRUISE_NEAREST_FUNC` (`ceil` for accel, `floor` for decel) instead of adding the delta directly — avoids overshooting when the current speed isn't already grid-aligned.
- Otherwise adds/subtracts `v_cruise_delta` per `CRUISE_INTERVAL_SIGN`.
- Special case: if the driver is pressing gas (`CS.gasPressed`) while pressing `decelCruise` or `setCruise`, clips the new set speed up to at least current `vEgo` (converted to kph) — comment: "If set is pressed while overriding, clip cruise speed to minimum of vEgo".
- Finally clips to `[V_CRUISE_MIN, V_CRUISE_MAX]` and rounds to 1 decimal (`np.clip(round(...), ...)`).

**`update_button_timers(self, CS, enabled)`** (`:114-124`): increments every currently-nonzero timer by 1 each frame (so timers count *frames held*, i.e. hundredths of a second at 100Hz); on any button press/release event for a tracked button, resets the timer to `1` (pressed) or `0` (released) and snapshots `button_change_states[type] = {"standstill": CS.cruiseState.standstill, "enabled": enabled}` at that instant — this snapshot is what the guards in `_update_v_cruise_non_pcm` consult later.

**`initialize_v_cruise(self, CS, experimental_mode)`** (`:126-138`) — called once per rising edge of `carControl.enabled` (from `card.py:183-185`), using the **previous** frame's `CarState` (so it sees the button event that actually triggered the enable):
- No-op if `CP.pcmCruise` (PCM handles its own initial set speed).
- Picks `initial = V_CRUISE_INITIAL_EXPERIMENTAL_MODE if experimental_mode else V_CRUISE_INITIAL`.
- If the triggering event was `accelCruise`/`resumeCruise` **and** a previous cruise speed exists (`v_cruise_initialized`), **restores** `v_cruise_kph_last` (resume-to-last-set-speed behavior) rather than reinitializing.
- Otherwise, sets `v_cruise_kph = clip(vEgo * MS_TO_KPH, initial, V_CRUISE_MAX)` rounded to an int — i.e. defaults to current speed, floored at the experimental/normal initial value and capped at max.
- Mirrors into `v_cruise_cluster_kph`.

### Testing (skim, `selfdrive/car/tests/test_cruise_speed.py`)

`TestCruiseSpeed` runs full longitudinal-maneuver simulations (`Maneuver`) across all `LongitudinalPersonality` values and both e2e/non-e2e, asserting the simulated vehicle actually reaches the requested cruise speed. `TestVCruiseHelper` (parameterized on `pcm_cruise=False` only — PCM path is explicitly marked `# TODO: test pcmCruise`, i.e. **not currently covered**) directly unit-tests `VCruiseHelper`: adjustment only on button release, no adjustment on rising-edge-of-enable, no increment when resuming from standstill, gas-pressed clip-to-vEgo behavior, and that `initialize_v_cruise` always lands in `[V_CRUISE_INITIAL, V_CRUISE_MAX]`.

## `selfdrive/car/car_specific.py` — `CarSpecificEvents`

### Purpose

Centralizes the (small amount of) genuinely brand-specific *event/alert* logic that doesn't belong inside each brand's `carstate.py`/`interface.py` — i.e. this is the one place in the otherwise-generic `card`/`selfdrived` pipeline that still branches on `CP.brand`. It does **not** run inside `card.py`'s loop; it's a helper class instantiated and driven by `selfdrived` (out of this section's scope; confirmed by import path — `card_specific.py` imports `openpilot.selfdrive.selfdrived.events.Events`, i.e. it depends on and is consumed by `selfdrived`, not the other way around). Documenting it here since it's explicitly in scope and it's the direct producer/consumer counterpart of the `CarState` fields `card.py` publishes.

### Class `CarSpecificEvents`

**`__init__(self, CP)`** (`:16-22`): stores `CP`; `steering_unpressed = 0` (frame counter since steering was last pressed); `low_speed_alert = False` (Chrysler-only latch); `no_steer_warning = False`, `silent_steer_warning = True` (hysteresis state for steer-fault alert severity).

**`update(self, CS, CS_prev, CC) -> Events`** (`:24-93`):
- Short-circuits to an empty `Events()` for `brand in ('body', 'mock')` (non-vehicle platforms).
- Always computes `events = self.create_common_events(CS, CS_prev)` first (see below), then layers brand-specific checks on top, branching on `self.CP.brand`:
  - **`chrysler`**: hysteresis for `belowSteerSpeed` around `minSteerSpeed` (enter alert below `minSteerSpeed+0.5`, clear above `minSteerSpeed+1.0` — a 0.5 kph/mph-scale deadband to avoid chattering).
  - **`honda`**: `belowEngageSpeed` if `pcmCruise` and under `minEnableSpeed`; PCM rising/falling-edge enable/disable logic distinct from the generic path (`create_common_events` explicitly excludes Honda from the generic `pcm_enable` branch, see below) — on PCM cruise disabling while openpilot is still engaged, adds `speedTooLow` (non-loud) if under `minEnableSpeed+2` else `cruiseDisabled`; `manualRestart` if `minEnableSpeed>0` and near-zero speed.
  - **`toyota`**: if `openpilotLongitudinalControl`, adds `resumeRequired` if standstill+not-braking+(`CC.cruiseControl.resume` or hybrid flag); adds `belowEngageSpeed` under `minEnableSpeed`, plus `speedTooLow` if commanded `accel > 0.3` (margin to avoid false-triggering while already stopping) and `manualRestart` if essentially stopped.
  - **`gm`**: `belowEngageSpeed` under `minEnableSpeed` unless standstill-with-firm-brake on a forward-camera-integrated car (allows first-time-stop engagement on some GMs per the `TODO` comment); `resumeRequired` if `cruiseState.standstill`.
  - **`volkswagen`**: if `openpilotLongitudinalControl`, `belowEngageSpeed` under `minEnableSpeed+0.5`; `speedTooLow` if enabled and under `minEnableSpeed`. A commented-out block (`:89-91`) references a not-yet-implemented `eps_timer_soft_disable_alert` — dead/aspirational code, clearly marked with a `TODO`.
  - All other brands: only the common events apply.

**`create_common_events(self, CS, CS_prev) -> Events`** (`:95-187`) — brand-agnostic checks run for every non-body/mock car:
- Looks up `CI = interfaces[self.CP.brand's carFingerprint]` to access `CI.DRIVABLE_GEARS` for the gear check (uses the **live interface class**, not a cached one — cheap dict lookup).
- `pcm_enable = CP.pcmCruise and CP.brand != 'honda'` — Honda is carved out here (handled instead in the honda branch of `update()` above) — annotated `# TODO: cleanup the honda-specific logic`.
- `allow_button_cancel = CP.brand != 'hyundai'` — annotated `# TODO: on some hyundai cars, the cancel button is also the pause/resume button, so only use it for cancel when running openpilot longitudinal`.
- Straightforward one-to-one flag→event mappings for: `doorOpen`, `seatbeltUnlatched`, `gearShifter` not drive/not in `DRIVABLE_GEARS` → `wrongGear`, `reverse` → `reverseGear`, `not cruiseState.available` → `wrongCarMode`, `espDisabled`, `espActive`, `stockFcw`, `stockAeb`, `stockLkas`, `vEgo > MAX_CTRL_SPEED` (imported from `opendbc.car.interfaces`) → `speedTooHigh`, `cruiseState.nonAdaptive` → `wrongCruiseMode`, `brakeHoldActive` (only if `openpilotLongitudinalControl`) → `brakeHold`, `parkingBrake` → `parkBrake`, `accFaulted`, `steeringPressed` → `steerOverride`, rising edge of `steeringDisengage` → `steerDisengage`, `brakePressed and standstill` → `preEnableStandstill`, `gasPressed` → `gasPressedOverride`, `vehicleSensorsInvalid`, `invalidLkasSetting`, `lowSpeedAlert` → `belowSteerSpeed`, `buttonEnable`.
- Cancel-button handling: adds `buttonCancel` for any `ButtonType.cancel` event, gated by `allow_button_cancel or not CP.pcmCruise`.
- Steering-fault hysteresis (`:159-177`) — the most stateful piece: tracks `steering_unpressed` (frames since last `steeringPressed`, reset to 0 whenever pressed, else incremented). On `steerFaultTemporary`:
  - If currently pressed and (the fault is new this frame, or already in "no-warning" mode), sets `no_steer_warning=True` (suppress the alert while the driver is actively holding the wheel through a fresh fault).
  - Otherwise `no_steer_warning=False`, and chooses alert severity: if already in "silent" mode, or standstill, or steering was released less than `1.5/DT_CTRL` frames ago (150 frames = 1.5s), emits the quieter `steerTempUnavailableSilent` and latches `silent_steer_warning=True`; else emits the louder `steerTempUnavailable`.
  - If no fault this frame, both `no_steer_warning` and `silent_steer_warning` reset to `False`.
  - `steerFaultPermanent` unconditionally adds `steerUnavailable`.
- Generic (non-Honda) PCM enable/disable edge detection (`:181-185`), only if `pcm_enable`: rising edge of `cruiseState.enabled` (and not `CS.blockPcmEnable`) → `pcmEnable`; falling edge (i.e. `not cruiseState.enabled`, checked every frame it's false, not just on edge — actually re-reading the code: `elif not CS.cruiseState.enabled: events.add(EventName.pcmDisable)` fires **every frame** cruise is disabled, not just on the transition frame — confirmed from code, this is *not* edge-gated the way the enable branch is).

### Discrepancy/uncertainty notes for this file

- The `pcmDisable` addition on line `:184-185` is unconditional while `cruiseState.enabled` is false (every frame), whereas `pcmEnable` on `:182-183` is edge-gated (`and not CS_prev.cruiseState.enabled`) — asymmetric by design or oversight is not stated in a comment; flagged as **confirmed from code, intent uncertain**. Since `Events`/alert dedup logic downstream (in `selfdrived`, out of scope) likely handles repeat events safely, this is probably benign but is a real asymmetry.
- Two `TODO` comments (`:59`, `:89`) mark known-incomplete brand logic (Toyota gear check should also exclude S1/S2/S3 states; VW's `eps_timer_soft_disable_alert` is unimplemented/commented out) — self-documented gaps, not silent bugs.

## `selfdrive/car/docs.py` and `CARS_template.md`

### `selfdrive/car/docs.py` (`:1-22`)

A thin CLI wrapper, **not** where the docs logic lives (that's `opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/docs.py`, out of exhaustive scope but read for context — see below). Defines `CARS_MD_OUT = <BASEDIR>/docs/CARS.md` and `CARS_MD_TEMPLATE = <BASEDIR>/selfdrive/car/CARS_template.md`; `__main__` block parses `--template`/`--out` overrides, calls `opendbc.car.docs.generate_cars_md(get_all_car_docs(), args.template)`, writes the result to `args.out`.

Notable duplication (confirmed, not a bug but worth flagging for reference accuracy): `opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/docs.py` **also** defines its own `EXTRA_CARS_MD_OUT`/`EXTRA_CARS_MD_TEMPLATE` pointing at paths *inside the opendbc repo itself* (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/docs/CARS.md` template-relative, resolved via `BASEDIR/../../docs/CARS.md`) and has its own `if __name__ == "__main__"` block that does the same generation using opendbc's own `CARS_template.md`. So there are **two independent entry points** that can regenerate a `CARS.md` from two different templates (`selfdrive/car/CARS_template.md` vs whatever lives under `opendbc/car/` if that file still exists in this checkout) — `selfdrive/car/tests/test_docs.py::test_generator` (`:15-16`) explicitly exercises the openpilot-level template (`CARS_MD_TEMPLATE` imported from `selfdrive.car.docs`) via the opendbc-level `generate_cars_md` function, i.e. openpilot's own test suite pins the openpilot-side template as the one that must stay renderable.

### `get_all_car_docs()` / `generate_cars_md()` (in `opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/docs.py`, read for context)

- `get_params_for_docs(platform)` (`:32-37`) calls the brand's `CarInterface.get_params(..., docs=True)` with an empty fingerprint and a single unknown-ECU `CarFw` entry — i.e. docs generation exercises the **same** `_get_params` code path every real car uses, just with synthetic/empty fingerprint data and the `docs=True` flag threaded through (brand code can use this flag to change docs-only defaults, e.g. always advertise a feature as available in docs even if it's normally fingerprint-gated).
- `build_sorted_car_docs_list` iterates all `Platform`s (plus `EXTRA` "community" platforms merged in via `ExtraPlatform = Platform | EXTRA`), collects each platform's `config.car_docs` entries (a platform can have >1 published `CarDocs`/model-year row), calls `.init_make(CP)`/`.init(CP, footnotes)` on each to populate the row cache, and naturally-sorts by name (accent-normalizing via NFKD so e.g. "Š" sorts with "S").
- `generate_cars_md` is a plain Jinja2 render (`trim_blocks=True, lstrip_blocks=True`) of the given template against the collected `CarDocs` list plus various enums (`PartType`, `Column`, `SupportType`, etc.) as template globals.

### `CARS_template.md` (what it generates — not treated as source of truth per task instructions)

Jinja2 template (`selfdrive/car/CARS_template.md:1-74`) that renders `docs/CARS.md`: a header count of `UPSTREAM`-support-type cars, one markdown table (columns driven by the `Column` enum, star-icon/video-icon helper macros, a widened "Hardware Needed" column via a zero-width spacer image trick), a footnotes section, and static prose about community-maintained cars, FlexRay-based brands that will likely never be supported (BMW/Mercedes/Audi/Land Rover/some Volvo), and a specific list of Toyota/Lexus models blocked by the "Toyota Security" message-authentication scheme (RAV4 Prime 2021+, Sienna 2021+, Venza 2021+, Sequoia 2023+, Tundra 2022+, Highlander 2024+, Corolla Cross 2022+ US, Camry 2025+, Lexus NX 2022+, bZ4x 2023+, Subaru Solterra 2023+). This list is static prose in the template, not derived from `CarDocs` data — i.e. maintained by hand and could drift from actual per-brand support state (**inferred risk**, not confirmed as currently stale).

## `selfdrive/car/tests/` (skimmed)

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `test_car_interfaces.py` | Property-based (Hypothesis) fuzz test, parameterized over **every** `PLATFORMS` entry plus `MOCK.MOCK`: builds a fuzzy `CarInterface` (`get_fuzzy_car_interface`, from `opendbc.car.tests.test_car_interfaces` — out of scope), feeds 10 frames of random `CarControl` with `enabled=False`-equivalent defaults then 10 more with `enabled=latActive=longActive=True`, calling `car_interface.update([])` / `.apply(CC, now_nanos)` each frame purely to check nothing throws; then instantiates `LongControl`, and one of `LatControlAngle`/`LatControlPID`/`LatControlTorque` depending on `steerControlType`/`lateralTuning.which()`, to sanity-check controller construction against the fuzz-generated `CarParams`. Explicitly notes (`Phase.target` excluded) that Hypothesis's targeted phase is too slow given how large `CarParams` (nested lists) is to shrink/target. |
| `test_cruise_speed.py` | Covered above under `cruise.py`. Also includes full closed-loop `Maneuver`-based cruise-speed-reaching tests, independent of the `VCruiseHelper` unit tests. |
| `test_docs.py` | `test_generator` just ensures the openpilot-level template renders without error; `test_docs_diff` dumps current `CarDocs` to a temp file and diffs against some reference/previous dump via `selfdrive/debug/dump_car_docs.py` / `print_docs_diff.py` (both out of scope), then deletes the dump — effectively a regression check that car-docs output doesn't silently change. |
| `test_models.py` | Large (out-of-scope-in-depth) route-replay-driven test: for each brand/platform, pulls real drive segments (`routes.py`), replays CAN through `can_capnp_to_list` and the actual `CarInterface`, and cross-checks against `opendbc.safety`'s compiled safety library (`libsafety_py`) — i.e. this is where the **Python-side car interface behavior is checked against the same safety rules the panda firmware enforces**, using segment-level real-world CAN logs rather than synthetic fuzzing. Supports job sharding (`NUM_JOBS`/`JOB_ID`) and both internal (comma-only) and public CI route sources. |
| `big_cars_test.sh` | Not read in detail (shell script, presumably a CI driver for `test_models.py` across the full car list) — **not analyzed**, out of scope depth. |

## The abstract `CarInterface` boundary (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/interfaces.py`)

Read to precisely describe what `card.py` programs against (per task scope — full per-brand semantics are out of scope; Toyota used below as the one worked example).

### `CarInterfaceBase(ABC)` (`interfaces.py:94-264`)

| Member | Kind | Signature / value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CarState`, `CarController` | class attrs | `type['CarStateBase']`, `type['CarControllerBase']` | Must be overridden by every brand subclass (assigned as plain class attributes, e.g. Toyota's `interface.py:14-15`) |
| `RadarInterface` | class attr | defaults to base `RadarInterfaceBase` | Overridable per brand |
| `DRIVABLE_GEARS` | class attr | `tuple[GearShifter, ...]`, default `()` | Consumed by `car_specific.py`'s `create_common_events` gear check |
| `__init__(self, CP)` (`:101-111`) | ctor | — | Stores `CP`; `frame=0`; `v_ego_cluster_seen=False`; instantiates `self.CS = self.CarState(CP)`; builds `self.can_parsers = self.CS.get_can_parsers(CP)` (dict of `StrEnum bus -> CANParser`); derives `dbc_names` per bus from those parsers; instantiates `self.CC = self.CarController(dbc_names, CP)` |
| `apply(self, c, now_nanos=None)` (`:113-116`) | method | `(structs.CarControl, int\|None) -> (Actuators, list[CanData])` | Thin wrapper: defaults `now_nanos` to wall clock, delegates to `self.CC.update(c, self.CS, now_nanos)`. This is exactly what `card.py:236` calls. |
| `get_pid_accel_limits(CP, current_speed, cruise_speed)` (`:118-120`) | staticmethod | `-> (float, float)` | Default `(ACCEL_MIN, ACCEL_MAX) = (-3.5, 2.0)`; brands override (Toyota overrides via `CarControllerParams`) |
| `get_non_essential_params(candidate)` (`:122-127`) | classmethod | `-> CarParams` | Calls `get_params` with empty fingerprint/no FW/no alpha-long/not release — used e.g. by `get_demo_car_params()` |
| `get_params(candidate, fingerprint, car_fw, alpha_long, is_release, docs)` (`:129-154`) | classmethod | `-> CarParams` | Builds `get_std_params(candidate)`, overlays platform spec constants (mass/wheelbase/steerRatio/etc. from `PLATFORMS[candidate]`), calls the brand's abstract `_get_params` to fill in the rest, adds `STD_CARGO_KG` to mass unless `notCar`, then derives `rotationalInertia`/tire stiffness via `scale_rot_inertia`/`scale_tire_stiffness`. **This is the function `get_car()` and the docs generator both call.** |
| `_get_params(...)` (`:156-160`) | abstract staticmethod | — | Brand-specific; must be implemented (Toyota's is the worked example below) |
| `init(CP, can_recv, can_send)` (`:162-164`) | staticmethod, overridable | — | Default no-op; used to disable longitudinal ECUs as needed. Called once by `card.py:229` |
| `deinit(CP, can_recv, can_send)` (`:166-168`) | staticmethod, overridable | — | Default no-op; re-enable ECUs. **Not called anywhere in `card.py`** — confirmed by grep of this section's files; likely invoked by `system/manager` on process shutdown (out of scope) — flagged as **uncertain** whether/where it's actually invoked in this checkout |
| `get_steer_feedforward_default` / `get_steer_feedforward_function` (`:170-176`) | static/method | — | Default feedforward proportional to `desired_angle * v_ego**2` |
| `torque_from_lateral_accel[_linear]` / `lateral_accel_from_torque[_linear]` / `*_from_torque()` (`:178-189`) | methods | — | Default linear torque↔lateral-accel model using `LateralTorqueTuning.latAccelFactor`; overridable per brand |
| `get_std_params(candidate)` (`:192-222`) | staticmethod | `-> CarParams` | Base defaults: `maxLateralAccel` from `get_torque_params()` table, `autoResumeSng=True`, `tireStiffnessFactor=1.0`, `steerControlType=torque`, `minSteerSpeed=0`, `wheelSpeedFactor=1.0`, `pcmCruise=True`, `minEnableSpeed=-1`, `openpilotLongitudinalControl=False`, `stopAccel=-2.0`, `stoppingDecelRate=0.8`, `vEgoStopping=vEgoStarting=0.5`, zeroed PID gains, `longitudinalActuatorDelay=0.15`, `steerLimitTimer=1.0` |
| `configure_torque_tune(candidate, tune, steering_angle_deadzone_deg=0.0)` (`:224-232`) | staticmethod | — | Populates a `LateralTorqueTuning` union member from the `torque_data/*.toml` tables (see `get_torque_params()` below) |
| `update(self, can_packets)` (`:234-264`) | method | `(list[tuple[int,list[CanData]]]) -> structs.CarState` | **The function `card.py`'s `Car.state_update` calls as `self.CI.update(can_list)`.** Runs every registered `CANParser.update(can_packets)`, then `ret = self.CS.update(self.can_parsers)` (brand-specific decode), sets `canValid`/`canTimeout` by ANDing/ORing all parsers' `can_valid`/`bus_timeout`, applies cluster-speed hysteresis/first-seen logic, defaults `cruiseState.speedCluster` to `cruiseState.speed` if zero, computes `buttonEnable` via `CS.update_button_enable`, and stashes `self.CS.out = ret` for next frame's hysteresis reference before returning `ret` |

`get_torque_params()` (`:48-75`, module-level, `@cache`d): loads three TOML files (`torque_data/params.toml`, `override.toml`, `substitute.toml`), builds a merged per-candidate dict of `{FRICTION, LAT_ACCEL_FACTOR, MAX_LAT_ACCEL_MEASURED}`-style fields (keyed off `params['legend']`), raising `RuntimeError` if a candidate is defined in more than one of the three tables, and `NotImplementedError` if a substituted candidate isn't found anywhere.

### `RadarInterfaceBase(ABC)` (`:80-91`)

Trivial default: `update(self, can_packets) -> structs.RadarDataT | None` increments `self.frame` and returns an **empty** `structs.RadarData()` every 5th call (`frame % 5 == 0`, comment "20 Hz is very standard"), else `None`. Brands with real radar decode (e.g. Toyota's `radar_interface.py`, not read in depth — out of scope) override this.

### `CarStateBase(ABC)` (`:267-360`)

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `__init__(self, CP)` (`:268-290`) | Stores `CP`/`car_fingerprint`; `self.out = structs.CarState()` (previous-frame cache); blinker/steering-press debounce counters all zeroed; `secoc_key` defaulted to 32 zero-bytes (`b"00"*16`, i.e. literally the two-character string `"00"` repeated 16 times — **note: this is a bytes literal `b"00"` repeated, producing a 32-*byte* object of ASCII `'0'`/`'0'` pairs, not 16 zero bytes** — worth flagging as a naming/intent subtlety, though it's just a placeholder overwritten by `card.py`'s real key loading when SecOC is required); constructs a 1D Kalman filter (`KF1D`) for speed smoothing with fixed `Q`/`R`/`A`/`C` matrices tied to `DT_CTRL` |
| `update(self, can_parsers) -> structs.CarState` | Abstract; brand-specific CAN decode |
| `parse_wheel_speeds(cs, fl, fr, rl, rr, unit=KPH_TO_MS)` (`:296-298`) | Averages 4 wheel speeds, applies `CP.wheelSpeedFactor`, feeds through `update_speed_kf` for `vEgo`/`aEgo` |
| `update_speed_kf(v_ego_raw)` (`:300-305`) | Resets the KF state if the raw reading jumps >2 m/s from the filter's current estimate (avoids a slow-converging filter fighting a real step change, e.g. at startup); else runs one KF update step |
| `update_blinker_from_lamp` / `update_blinker_from_stalk` (`:307-342`) | Two different blinker-debounce strategies (lamp-state-based countdown timer vs. stalk-position-based with rising-edge reset and cross-cancellation) — brands pick whichever matches their signal source |
| `update_steering_pressed(pressed, min_count)` (`:315-319`) | Symmetric up/down counter clipped to `[0, 2*min_count+1]`, returns `True` once the counter exceeds `min_count` — a debounce filter against noisy driver-torque signals |
| `update_button_enable(buttonEvents)` (`:344-350`) | Only meaningful when `not CP.pcmCruise`: returns `True` on falling edge of `accelCruise`/`decelCruise` (the "openpilot-native enable" signal, published as `CarState.buttonEnable` and consumed by `car_specific.py`'s common events) |
| `parse_gear_shifter(gear)` (`:352-356`, static) | String→`GearShifter` enum via `GEAR_SHIFTER_MAP` (`:32-42`), `unknown` if `None`/unrecognized |
| `get_can_parsers(CP)` (`:358-360`, static) | Default returns `{}`; brands override to build their real `CANParser`s per bus |

### `CarControllerBase(ABC)` (`:363-371`)

Minimal: `__init__(self, dbc_names, CP)` stores `CP`, `frame=0`, `secoc_key` placeholder; abstract `update(self, CC, CS, now_nanos) -> (Actuators, list[CanData])` — brand-specific CAN encode, this is exactly what `CarInterfaceBase.apply()` delegates to and thus what `card.py` ultimately calls every `carControl`-driven frame.

### `get_interface_attr(attr, combine_brands=False, ignore_none=False)` (`:382-405`)

Utility used elsewhere in opendbc (e.g. `car_specific.py`'s use of `interfaces[...]` is a different mechanism — this function instead walks every folder under `opendbc/car/`, dynamically imports `opendbc.car.<brand>.values` (or `.fingerprints` for `FINGERPRINTS`/`FW_VERSIONS`), and pulls out a named attribute per brand — swallows `ImportError`/`OSError` per folder. Not directly used by `card.py`, included here because `docs.py` (`get_all_footnotes`) relies on it.

### Toyota as the representative brand implementation (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/toyota/interface.py`, 138 lines, fully read)

`CarInterface(CarInterfaceBase)`:
- Wires `CarState`/`CarController`/`RadarInterface` to Toyota's concrete classes; `DRIVABLE_GEARS = (GearShifter.sport,)` (Toyota's "S" gear position counts as drivable, in addition to the generic `drive` check in `car_specific.py`).
- `get_pid_accel_limits` overridden to pull brand-tuned `ACCEL_MIN`/`ACCEL_MAX` off `CarControllerParams(CP)` instead of the generic `-3.5/2.0`.
- `_get_params` (`:24-124`) — representative of how much a real brand's `_get_params` does versus the generic base: sets `brand`/`safetyConfigs` (`SafetyModel.toyota`, `safetyParam = EPS_SCALE[candidate]`, OR'd with `ALT_BRAKE`/`SECOC`/`LTA`/`STOCK_LONGITUDINAL` flag bits depending on detected DBC/ECU/candidate); SecOC cars get `secOcRequired=True` and (if `is_release`) `dashcamOnly=True` (SecOC support gated to non-release builds only, at least in this checkout — **confirmed from code**); angle-control cars (`ANGLE_CONTROL_CAR`) get `steerControlType=angle` with different `steerActuatorDelay`/`steerLimitTimer`, else calls the base `configure_torque_tune`; per-model `stop_and_go` overrides (Prius, Lexus RX variants, Avalon-by-year, several others); detects hybrid ECU presence from `car_fw` to set `ToyotaFlags.HYBRID`; sets `enableBsm` from a fingerprint-bit heuristic gated to `TSS2_CAR`; `radarUnavailable` from whether the brand's DBC has a `Bus.radar` entry; for `RADAR_ACC_CAR`s, advertises `alphaLongitudinalAvailable=True` and, if the alpha-long toggle is on, sets a `DISABLE_RADAR` flag; derives `openpilotLongitudinalControl` from whether the car is TSS2-minus-radar-ACC or has the disable-radar flag, and sets `STOCK_LONGITUDINAL` safety flag when it's *not* doing OP longitudinal; sets `minEnableSpeed` to `-1` (unrestricted) if `stop_and_go` else a brand constant `MIN_ACC_SPEED`; TSS2 cars get relaxed stopping/starting speeds and a `RAISED_ACCEL_LIMIT` flag, with hybrids getting a much shorter `longitudinalActuatorDelay` (0.05s vs default 0.15s).
- `init`/`deinit` (`:126-138`) — the concrete example of `CarInterfaceBase.init`/`deinit` doing real work: if `ToyotaFlags.DISABLE_RADAR` is set (alpha-long toggled on a radar-ACC car), sends a UDS `COMMUNICATION_CONTROL` request over `can_send`/`can_recv` to `disable_ecu(..., addr=0x750, sub_addr=0xf, ...)` to silence the radar's CAN transmissions (`ENABLE_RX_DISABLE_TX`) on `init`, and the inverse (`ENABLE_RX_ENABLE_TX`) on `deinit` — this is the call `card.py:229` (`self.CI.init(self.CP, *self.can_callbacks)`) triggers for these specific cars, and confirms the earlier note that `deinit` exists in the base class for symmetry even though this section's files never call it (Toyota implements it correctly regardless, presumably for whatever out-of-scope caller does invoke it, e.g. on manager shutdown).
